sampling_model.design: Fixed finite family of perfect-intervention settings \(v=(S,x)\), where \(x=0\) or a unit coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^S\).
sampling_model.units: For the statistical rung, \(m\) independent equilibrium observations are drawn in every retained setting; population identification uses the full response kernels.
sampling_model.treatment: A treatment sets every observed coordinate in \(S\) to \(x\) and preserves the remaining equations and source laws.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed because regimes are designed; every retained regime has \(m\) draws.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No source separation is performed. Empirical characteristic functions at \(J_m\) computable rational frequencies are compared with globally certified compact-model characteristic functions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For irreducible latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, observational distribution equivalence is characterized by equality of children-basis families up to a vertex permutation.
Latent directed acyclic graphs are hard-intervention equivalent exactly when their intervention-indexed augmented maximal ancestral graphs satisfy the stated skeleton and collider criteria.
The pair condition together with the covariance condition is necessary and sufficient for full recovery of a linear cyclic model from experimental means and covariances.

Proposition 5.1 states that the observational distribution together with the atomic interventional distribution for coordinate \(i\) recovers row \(i\) of the square coefficient matrix, hence its parents and causal effects.
Aligned single-target equilibrium response maps identify a latent cyclic mechanism under full target coverage, with a graph-dependent characterization when one target is missing.
Cross-cumulant tensor rank restrictions yield goodness-of-fit tests for latent linear non-Gaussian structural equation models.
Inverting graph-indexed goodness-of-fit tests yields asymptotically valid confidence sets for causal orderings in acyclic additive-error models.

body.tldr: The paper characterizes when two exact-support linear non-Gaussian feedback graphs with a fixed number of latent nodes generate exactly the same joint family of perfect-intervention response kernels. The kernel combines an exact affine and Hall--Rado realization theorem for observed mixing matrices, a finite visible-source partition theorem that eliminates arbitrary source laws, and simultaneous principal-response constraints imposed by one common mechanism. An effective sign-invariant chart compiler and a common-lift theorem expose the genuine open content. The internal square no-latent reduction derives the projection, lift, row-recovery map, and matching-set equality while matching Sharifian et al. only on their published row-recovery clause; a four-node all-parameter witness proves strict refinement over observational equivalence, and a bounded-Laplace characteristic-function inversion supplies an honest graph confidence superset without latent-source recovery.

project_justification.gap: Existing results separately characterize observational law-set equivalence for latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, graphical intervention equivalence for latent directed acyclic graphs, or full parameter recovery under sufficiently rich second-order experiments. None gives an exact all-cancellations criterion for equality of full affine response-kernel model sets when the graph is exact structural support and one coefficient matrix and source-law tuple must serve every regime.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a finite coupled invariant that simultaneously represents punctured structural completion, invisible or merged independent sources, principal intervention responses, and common-mechanism gluing on every lower-dimensional stratum.
project_justification.fill: The proposed criterion reduces admissible mechanisms to graph-generated affine and rank charts, reduces arbitrary source-law containment to finite proportional-column surjections, couples regimes through principal response matrices, and asks for an explicit certified compiler with a size-dependent bit bound. The inferential rung compares observable characteristic functions directly on a compact subclass.

body.related_work: Dai et al., Theorem 2, motivate a graph-generated equivalence object for latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, but that theorem concerns observational distribution sets under a zero-allowed support convention and does not settle the exact-support intervention problem. Zhou et al. encode hard-intervention invariances for latent directed acyclic graphs through augmented maximal ancestral graphs; their object is graphical constraint equivalence rather than equality of cyclic parametric response-kernel sets. Bongers et al. supply the solvability semantics that justify imposing invertibility separately after every intervention; the stronger uniform singular-value margin used only in the inference subclass is not their assumption or result. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer give necessary and sufficient experiment-design conditions for full second-order recovery, which is a different target from the quotient under an arbitrary fixed intervention family. Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, establish published row recovery for coordinate \(i\) in a square no-latent model from observational and randomized atomic-intervention distributions. Separately, the internal node \(\texttt{thm:no-latent-reduction}\), proposal Theorem 5, supplies the square projection, lift, response-kernel row-recovery map, and matching-set equality; only its row-recovery clause matches Proposition 5.1. Taeb et al. and Joint Causal Inference make shared mechanisms across environments explicit, but do not provide the required cyclic non-Gaussian common-lift theorem. Dadgostari and Nazemi study aligned response matrices for sensing an entirely latent equilibrium state and identify a single mechanism under target coverage or support conditions; they do not compare graph-indexed full-law sets under observed-node perfect interventions, arbitrary independent sources, and exact cancellations. Schkoda and Drton provide rank-based goodness-of-fit tests, while Wang, Kolar, and Drton provide test inversion for acyclic orderings; the statistical rung instead tests full observable law-set proximity for compact latent feedback models.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The affine and Hall--Rado realization criterion has passed forced-zero, latent-rank, degenerate-pivot, and exact rational witness checks at \(N=4\), but these finite checks do not prove the universal punctured-affine selection theorem. The source-partition argument still requires a full audit of finite-support measure equality in the original jump lattice and non-Gaussian closure after merging. The population compiler must handle every lower-dimensional cell and produce its own explicit complexity bound. The displayed strict-refinement witness does not establish failure of independent regime-wise equivalence; that stronger issue remains Open-ended Question 2.
body.honest_scope: The intervention pushforward identity, finite checks, and explicit witness provide proof architecture, not settled results. The sound-and-complete chart theorem, source-factorization theorem, effective compiler, common-lift boundary, internal no-latent projection, lift and matching-set equality, and statistical certification are all stated as claims to prove. Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, supplies only the published row-recovery comparator. The theorem is uniform over each finite input size but does not range over unbounded latent cardinality in one run. Under \(\ell=0\), the observational projection equals the square perfect-matching object, and the atomic projection restricts it by the recovered row labels. No strict-extension corollary to Dai et al.'s zero-allowed observational class is asserted because that class permits coefficient-zero strata and omits the coupled intervention object, so its graph-indexed equivalence relation is not the same ordered model-class comparison.
